result.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: group.js findMembers computes `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`, which allows offset == user_count. removeMember then calls `self.findMembers()` with the stale pre-removal user_count (e.g. 51) while offset is 50; the server (groups_controller members action) returns the new total of 50 with offset 50 and an empty member list. totalPages = floor(50/50)+1 = 2 and currentPage = 2, so the admin sees an empty '2/2' page with no automatic page-step back — the mechanism described in the finding holds exactly.

judged_text: findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, offset), which permits offset == user_count — a page past the last member — instead of capping at user_count - limit. Removing the last member while the final page holds exactly one member (e.g. a 51-member group on page 2) reloads with offset still at 50 against a new total of 50, leaving the admin staring at an empty '2/2' member list until they manually click 'previous'.
